25847-patty-s-friends.title: Patty'S Friends
25847-patty-s-friends.creator: Carolyn Wells
25847-patty-s-friends.description: A book by Carolyn Wells. "So I could go to two places at once. Here I have two lovely invitations for this afternoon, and I don't know which I want to accept most. One is a musicale at Mrs. Hastings', and the other is a picture exhibition at the New Gallery."

arxiv-1802-06271.title: Lower Bounds on Sparse Spanners, Emulators, and Diameter-reducing Shortcuts Journal: TALG CCS: Theory of computation Sparsification and spanners
arxiv-1802-06271.creator: Shang-En Huang, Seth Pettie
arxiv-1802-06271.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Shang-En Huang, Seth Pettie. We prove better lower bounds on additive spanners and emulators, which are lossy compression schemes for undirected graphs, as well as lower bounds on shortcut sets , which reduce the diameter of directed graphs.

arxiv-2105-08894.title: Physical Characterization of Serendipitously Uncovered Millimeter-wave Line-emitting Galaxies at z ∼ 2.5 z\sim 2.5 behind the Local Luminous Infrared Galaxy VV 114 Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2105-08894.creator: Shoichiro Mizukoshi, Kotaro Kohno, Fumi Egusa, Bunyo Hatsukade, Takeo Minezaki, Toshiki Saito, Yoichi Tamura, Daisuke Iono, Junko Ueda, Yuichi Matsuda, Ryohei Kawabe, Minju M. Lee, Min S. Yun, Daniel Espada
arxiv-2105-08894.description: Abstract We present a detailed investigation of millimeter-wave line emitters ALMA J010748.3-173028 (ALMA-J0107a) and ALMA J010747.0-173010 (ALMA-J0107b), which were serendipitously uncovered in the background of the nearby galaxy VV 114 with spectral scan observations at λ \lambda = 2 – 3 mm.

arxiv-2111-15572.title: Drop impact onto a substrate wetted by anotherliquid: Corona detachment from the wall film
arxiv-2111-15572.creator: Bastian Stumpf, Ilia V. Roisman, Alexander L. Yarin, Cameron Tropea
arxiv-2111-15572.description: Abstract Drop impact onto a thin liquid film of another liquid is observed and characterized using a high-speed video system. A new mode of splash - a complete, simultaneous corona detachment - has been observed, which is the result of the lamella breakup near the wall film.

arxiv-2210-09661.title: A crack in the track of the Hubble constant Thanks: Citation : Forthcoming in Philosophy of Astrophysics , Springer, Synthese Library, eds. N.Boyd, S. De Baerdemaeker, V. Matarese and K. Heng.
arxiv-2210-09661.creator: Marie Gueguen
arxiv-2210-09661.description: Abstract Measuring the rate at which the universe expands at a given time–the ‘Hubble constant’– has been a topic of controversy since the first measure of its expansion by Edwin Hubble in the 1920’s. As early as the 1970’s, Sandage et de Vaucouleurs have been arguing about the adequate methodology for such a measurement.

arxiv-2305-07804.title: Improving Small Language Models on PubMedQA via Generative Data Augmentation
arxiv-2305-07804.creator: Zhen Guo, Yanwei Wang, Peiqi Wang, Shangdi Yu
arxiv-2305-07804.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have made remarkable advancements in the field of natural language processing. However, their increasing size poses challenges in terms of computational cost. On the other hand, Small Language Models (SLMs) are known for their efficiency, but they often struggle with limited capacity and training data, especially in specific domains.

arxiv-2305-08768.title: An Introduction to String Diagrams for Computer Scientists
arxiv-2305-08768.creator: Robin Piedeleu, Fabio Zanasi
arxiv-2305-08768.description: Abstract \CUPseries \CUPelements keywords string diagrams \copyrightauthor Robin Piedeleu and Fabio Zanasi, 2023 1 The Case for String Diagrams The algebraic structure of programs When learning a programming language, one of the most basic tasks is understanding how to correctly write programs in the language syntax . This syntax is often specified inductively, as a context-free grammar.

arxiv-2410-22080.title: A New Broadcast Primitive for BFT Protocols
arxiv-2410-22080.creator: Manu Drijvers 1 , Tim Gretler , Yotam Harchol 3∗ , Tobias Klenze ∗ , Ognjen Maric 1 , Stefan Neamtu ∗ , Yvonne-Anne Pignolet 1 , Rostislav Rumenov 1 , Daniel Sharifi 1 , Victor Shoup 3∗ 1 DFINITY Foundation, 2 NVIDIA, 3 Offchain Labs manu@dfinity.org , gretler.tim@gmail.com , yotam@cs.berkeley.edu ,
arxiv-2410-22080.description: Abstract Byzantine fault tolerant (BFT) protocol descriptions often assume application-layer networking primitives, such as best-effort and reliable broadcast, which are impossible to implement in practice in a Byzantine environment as they require either unbounded buffering of messages or giving up liveness, under certain circumstances.

arxiv-2411-10606.title: AmoebaLLM: Constructing Any-Shape Large Language Models for Efficient and Instant Deployment
arxiv-2411-10606.creator: Yonggan Fu, Zhongzhi Yu, Junwei Li, Jiayi Qian, Yongan Zhang, Xiangchi Yuan
arxiv-2411-10606.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yonggan Fu, Zhongzhi Yu, Junwei Li, Jiayi Qian, Yongan Zhang, Xiangchi Yuan. Motivated by the transformative capabilities of large language models (LLMs) across various natural language tasks, there has been a growing demand to deploy these models effectively across diverse real-world applications and platforms. However, the challenge of efficiently deploying LLMs has become increasingly pronounced due to the varying application-specific performance requirements and the rapid evolution of computational platforms, which feature diverse resource constraints and deployment flows.

arxiv-2502-02679.title: Networks with Finite VC Dimension: Pro and Contra
arxiv-2502-02679.creator: Věra Kůrková, Marcello Sanguineti
arxiv-2502-02679.description: Abstract Neural networks are expected both to learn from data and to approximate task-relevant functions with sufficient accuracy. While finite Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) dimension provides a classical guarantee of learnability through polynomial growth of the hypothesis class and uniform convergence of empirical errors, its implications for approximation accuracy have not been systematically examined.

arxiv-2502-19297.title: Combining Planning and Reinforcement Learning for Solving Relational Multiagent Domains
arxiv-2502-19297.creator: Nikhilesh Prabhakar, Ranveer Singh, Harsha Kokel, Sriraam Natarajan, Prasad Tadepalli
arxiv-2502-19297.description: Abstract . Multiagent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) poses significant challenges due to the exponential growth of state and action spaces and the non-stationary nature of multiagent environments. This results in notable sample inefficiency and hinders generalization across diverse tasks. The complexity is further pronounced in relational settings, where domain knowledge is crucial but often underutilized by existing MARL algorithms.

arxiv-2505-00810.title: Scalable Unit Harmonization in Medical Informatics Using Bi-directional Transformers and Bayesian-Optimized BM25 and Sentence Embedding Retrieval
arxiv-2505-00810.creator: Jordi de la Torre
arxiv-2505-00810.description: Abstract Objective: To develop and evaluate a scalable methodology for harmonizing inconsistent units in large-scale clinical datasets, addressing a key barrier to data interoperability. Materials and Methods: We designed a novel unit harmonization system combining BM25, sentence embeddings, Bayesian optimization, and a bidirectional transformer based binary classifier for retrieving and matching laboratory test entries.

arxiv-2507-22070.title: Automated Test Data Generation for Enterprise Protobuf Systems: A Metaclass-Enhanced Statistical Approach
arxiv-2507-22070.creator: Y. Du
arxiv-2507-22070.description: Abstract Large-scale enterprise systems utilizing Protocol Buffers (protobuf) present significant challenges for performance testing, particularly when targeting intermediate business interfaces with complex nested data structures. Traditional test data generation approaches are inadequate for handling the intricate hierarchical and graph-like structures inherent in enterprise protobuf schemas.

arxiv-2510-19124.title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory for Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows and Fluctuations
arxiv-2510-19124.creator: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, Vojtěch Vlček
arxiv-2510-19124.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, Vojtěch Vlček. We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems, that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations. Two new Feynman rules render the evaluation of dissipative diagrams compact and systematically improvable, while preserving the Keldysh and anti-Hermitian symmetries of the closed-system theory.

britannica-1911-clauberg-johann.title: Clauberg, Johann (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-clauberg-johann.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-clauberg-johann.description: Article 'Clauberg, Johann' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 6), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born at Solingen, in Westphalia, on the 24th of February 1622. After travelling in France and England, he studied the Cartesian philosophy under John Raey at Leiden. He became (1649) professor of philosophy and theology at Herborn, but subsequently (1651), in consequence of the jealousy of his colleagues, accepted an invitation to a similar post at Duisburg, where he died on the 31st of January 1665.

pmc-10506899.title: Clinical Characteristics of Gynecologic Problems During Childhood in the Korean Population
pmc-10506899.creator: Haewon Choi, Sung Eun Kim, Nae Hyun Lee, Dong-Yun Lee, DooSeok Choi
pmc-10506899.description: BackgroundThis study analyzed common gynecologic problems among Korean patients younger than ten years.MethodsWe performed a retrospective analysis of medical records of patients younger than ten years who visited the Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology Clinic at Samsung Medical Center between 1995 and 2020.

pmc-10594049.title: Novel five-phase model for understanding the nature of misophonia, a conditioned aversive reflex disorder
pmc-10594049.creator: Thomas Dozier, Nathanael Mitchell, Jordan Norris, Jeyasakthy Saniasiaya, Thomas Dozier, Jordan Norris, Thomas Dozier, Jadon Webb, Jadon Webb, Thomas Dozier
pmc-10594049.description: Background: Misophonia is a recently identified condition in which a person perceives a subtle stimulus (e.g., eating sounds, hair twirling) and has an intense, negative emotional response. Misophonia cannot be classified with established nosological systems. Methods: We present a novel five-phase model of misophonia from a cognitive-behavioral framework.

pmc-10607116.title: Cannabidiol Modulates Emotional Function and Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Expression in Middle-Aged Female Rats Exposed to Social Isolation
pmc-10607116.creator: Nadya Saad, Danielle Raviv, Tomer Mizrachi Zer-Aviv, Irit Akirav
pmc-10607116.description: Aging is associated with changes in cognitive and emotional function. Cannabidiol (CBD) has been reported to attenuate stress and anxiety in human and animal studies. In this study, we aimed to assess the therapeutic potential of CBD among middle-aged female rats exposed to social isolation (SI) and the potential involvement of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in these effects.

pmc-10647170.title: Tongue Mucoceles: a retrospective clinic-pathological evaluation of 240 cases
pmc-10647170.creator: Romeo Patini, Michele Giuliani, Gioele Gioco, Mariateresa Tranfa, Vito Carlo Alberto Caponio, John Fantasia, Carlo Lajolo
pmc-10647170.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundMinor salivary glands can be found in the ventral and anterior part of the tongue; these glands can rarely develop mucoceles that, due to their rarity and their unusual clinical appearance, may present an interesting differential diagnosis. Mucoceles appear as an exophytic, sometimes pedunculated, lesion, which is a feature that is due to the absence of a capsule; thus, the glands are right beneath the mucosa and over the muscle tissue.

pmc-10727816.title: An ever-increasing metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease-related hepatocellular carcinoma: what are problems and countermeasures?
pmc-10727816.creator: Shigeo Shimose, Tsubasa Tsutsumi, Dan Nakano, Tomoya Sano, Keisuke Amano, Takumi Kawaguchi
pmc-10727816.description: ce of non-viral HCC is increasing and fatty liver is becoming a major etiology for the HCC. In 2020, a new concept of fatty liver disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), was proposed by the International Expert Panel consisting of 32 specialists from 22 countries (2,3).

pmc-11475842.title: StratosPHere 2: study protocol for a response-adaptive randomised placebo-controlled phase II trial to evaluate hydroxychloroquine and phenylbutyrate in pulmonary arterial hypertension caused by mutations in BMPR2
pmc-11475842.creator: Nina Deliu, Rajenki Das, Angelique May, Joseph Newman, Jo Steele, Melissa Duckworth, Rowena J Jones, Martin R Wilkins, Mark R Toshner, Sofia S Villar
pmc-11475842.description: BackgroundPulmonary arterial hypertension is a life-threatening progressive disorder characterised by high blood pressure (hypertension) in the arteries of the lungs (pulmonary artery). Although treatable, there is no known cure for this rare disorder, and its exact cause is unknown. Mutations in the bone morphogenetic protein receptor type-2 (BMPR2) are the most common genetic cause of familial pulmonary arterial hypertension.

pmc-11539719.title: Flexible and scalable photothermal/electro thermal anti-icing/de-icing metamaterials for effective large-scale preparation
pmc-11539719.creator: Tonghui Lu, Xianglin Li, Mengying Lu, Wenhao Lv, Wenzhuo Liu, Xuanchen Dong, Zhe Liu, Shangzhen Xie, Song Lv
pmc-11539719.description: SummaryAnti-icing and de-icing are vital for infrastructure maintenance. While carbon-based materials with photothermal or electrothermal effects have advanced, they face challenges like environmental dependence, poor resistance, high energy consumption, and complex manufacturing. Here, we developed a scalable, hybrid metamaterial driven by photothermal/electrothermal for all-weather anti-icing/de-icing.

pmc-11603254.title: Safety and Efficacy of Jenacid® Herbal Product Against Indomethacin-Induced Ulcers in Albino Wistar Rats
pmc-11603254.creator: Joshua Kiprotich, Neeza Timothy, Tadele M Yadesa, Daniel C Mwandah
pmc-11603254.description: Background: Jenacid Herbal Product (JHP) used for treating peptic ulcer disease in Uganda, sold over the counter, is approved by the National Drug Authority as a Traditional Herbal Product number THP 482. There have been no published studies on its safety and efficacy.Objective: This study aimed to assess potential acute and subacute toxicity as well as the efficacy of JHP.

pmc-11658269.title: Circular RNA circPHLPP2 promotes tumor growth and anti-PD-1 resistance through binding ILF3 to regulate IL36γ transcription in colorectal cancer
pmc-11658269.creator: Yan Hu, Ze-Rong Cai, Ren-Ze Huang, De-Shen Wang, Huai-Qiang Ju, Dong-Liang Chen
pmc-11658269.description: BackgroundMost Colorectal Cancer (CRC) patients exhibit limited responsiveness to anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) therapy, with the underlying mechanisms remaining elusive. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) play a significant role in tumorigenesis and development, with potential applications in tumor screening and predicting treatment efficacy. However, there are few studies exploring the role of circRNAs in CRC immune evasion.

pmc-11718110.title: Programmable Valve With Virtual off Function Is Useful for Chronic Subdural Hematoma After Ventriculoperitoneal Shunt Surgery
pmc-11718110.creator: Kento Tsuburaya, Takashi Matsumori, Masashi Uchida, Hiroshi Takasuna, Hidetoshi Murata
pmc-11718110.description: Over-drainage after a ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt can often lead to chronic subdural hematoma; however, the treatment is unclear. Hematoma drainage is performed after physically stopping the shunt function, such as by ligating or removing the shunt system. However, shunt reconstruction is required after the subdural hematoma improves.

pmc-12369232.title: Metal-organic frameworks activate the cGAS-STING pathway for cancer immunotherapy
pmc-12369232.creator: Shuxuan Zhu, Wenfei Xu, Hongxia Li, Zhaogang Sun, Ying Zhu, Wenjing Liu, Hongqian Chu
pmc-12369232.description: Despite the major breakthroughs in immunotherapy, a substantial number of cancer patients continue to confront problems such as low response rates, which restrict the overall effectiveness of existing treatments. There is an urgent necessity to combine advanced biomedical advancements with conventional therapies to improve treatment results.

pmc-12611492.title: Association of the triglyceride-glucose index with cardiovascular outcomes across cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages
pmc-12611492.creator: Byung Sik Kim, Hyun-Jin Kim, Shinje Moon, Hasung Kim, Jungkuk Lee, Jeong-Hun Shin
pmc-12611492.description: Background/AimsCardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome reflects the interplay between metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Insulin resistance (IR) is a key driver of CKM and is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a cost-effective surrogate marker of IR; however, its prognostic value across CKM syndrome stages remains unclear.

pmc-12618293.title: Balancing yield and stability: optimizing leaf pigment extraction to minimize chlorophyll degradation
pmc-12618293.creator: Monika Sitarek-Andrzejczyk, Jakub Dobrzyński, Paweł Orliński, Jarosław L. Przybył
pmc-12618293.description: Main conclusionMethanol proved to be the most efficient solvent for pigment extraction using pressurized liquid extraction, while extraction temperature and static time critically influenced both the yield and stability of the pigments.AbstractPhotosynthetic pigments, particularly chlorophylls and carotenoids, are central to plant physiology and are increasingly valued for their nutritional and functional benefits in the human diet.

pmc-12820335.title: Efficient perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 tandem solar cells with a composite intermediate recombination layer
pmc-12820335.creator: Wang Li, Junjun Zhang, Li Zeng, Wanhai Wang, Zhou Fang, Xinxing Liu, Zengyang Ma, Yitian Zhang, Hui Yan, Chen Shen, Zhuo Xue, Jingyi Zhu, Qiren Luo, Chang Liu, Ruixuan Jiang, Tongle Bu, Weihua Tang, Jianmin Li, Sheng Wang, Junbo Gong, Xudong Xiao
pmc-12820335.description: Monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells offer unique advantages among tandem configurations, including optimal bandgap pairing, all-thin-film architecture, superior radiation hardness, and exceptional stability. Despite their potential, challenges remain in optimizing efficiency and stability, particularly in the intermediate recombination layer (IRL) that connects subcells.

pmc-12964246.title: Tumor metabolic plasticity in therapy resistance: from the Warburg effect to mitochondrial hijacking
pmc-12964246.creator: Yen-Dun Tony Tzeng, Emmanuel Naveen Raj, Shih-Hsuan Cheng, Su-Boon Yong, Shih-Chieh Lin, Ren-Wang Peng, Chia-Jung Li
pmc-12964246.description: The clinical efficacy of targeted cancer therapies is persistently undermined by the emergence of acquired resistance. While secondary genetic mutations are well-characterized, increasing evidence implicates non-genetic metabolic reprogramming as a primary driver of survival during the initial phase of treatment.
